content.content:
Fred,

I'm in LA from tomorrow for Dentsu and the Griffin AGM, so can you take over the vendor and partner backlog this week? That's anyone outside the investor work who has an offer, a trial, a quote, terms or an ask in front of us and that one of us has actually engaged with: a call, a reply, a sign-up or paper. Cold pitches nobody answered, including ones we only forwarded around internally, stay off it, and so do the ad networks, PlayableX, Craftsman+ and Singular (they all stay on the UA budget call), the investors, and Mattel, which I'm keeping.

Go by the runway guardrails doc for what we do with each one, plus the one change I posted in #executives on Monday. Anything that needs signing goes the way ESG's note about signing says.

Everyone who is waiting to hear from us should get a written answer this week. Get each company's contact into Contacts so we're not digging through mail next time.

Log it all in a sheet in the Q4 commitments folder, the README in the folder has the columns. Then reply here with what we're keeping and what's waiting on Arthur or me to sign.

Thanks,
Leonard

{"documentId": "f_b98287f6f80fe431a71209", "title": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "name": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "revisionId": "0d3b4ff7c7", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T16:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "text": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments
Leonard, Sep 26. Until we know where the raise lands, this is how we handle anything outside the investor work that wants money, a signature or an answer from us.
How to decide
Go top to bottom and stop at the first one that fits.
1. Already answered. If one of us has already given them an answer, don't write to them again. Note who answered and when. If the answer was "later", it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars too.
2. Cash test. Anything that would cost us cash between Oct 1 and Dec 31 ends now: say no, or cancel it in writing the way their paper or notice asks. A trial or pilot that turns into a paid plan inside that window counts as cash, and so does an offer we would have to take up and pay for before January. Travel and event costs count only when we book them ourselves.
3. Keep. The cash test has one exception: anything on Arthur's keep-running list on our board stays, even if it costs money. Tell them we're staying.
4. Sign. If it costs nothing before January but taking it means someone has to accept terms or sign for the company, it goes the way ESG's note says. Tell them it's with Leonard or Arthur to sign, and with our lawyers first when ESG has to see it.
5. Park. Everything else that's free until January, including offers we could still take up after that. Tell them we'll pick it up in January; it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars (first week of January).
Answers
Everyone who is waiting to hear from us gets a written answer. Portals and no-reply notices don't need one.
"}

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Hi Leonard,

Following up on our call today, here's how we'd like agreements handled from now on while you're raising:

- Only an officer, you or Arthur, accepts terms or signs for Harmony Games, whatever the amount. That includes click-through terms and portal NDAs.
- Anything with an automatic renewal, exclusivity, a licence of your IP or a term over 12 months comes to us before anyone signs. Send each one to our intake address (it's in your Contacts as ESG Law intake), one email per agreement, so we can open a matter for it.
- Mutual NDAs on our template don't need review, whatever their term. An officer can sign them.

Best,
PERSON_2694_NAME
PARTNER, ESG Law
Agreed. This replaces what I said in July about Fred signing small stuff himself.

Fred, Arthur: anything waiting on Arthur or me to sign, put it on our founders' board To Do list with the company's name in the card title, including the ones that go to ESG. For the intake emails, what to include is in the intake checklist I shared.

Leonard

content.content:
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for applying to the Lumencloud Startup Program. Good news, Harmony Games qualifies for $25,000 in Lumencloud credits. The program agreement is attached; it's a 36-month term and the credits start once it's signed. Applications for this cohort close Oct 31.

Aiden
====
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for the call on Wednesday. We'd like to feature Zombie Match 3D in our November puzzle week. The featuring agreement has to be accepted in our partner portal by an authorised signatory of the company. No fees. Could that happen by Oct 24?

Mateo
====
Hi Frederick,

Following our call, the letter of intent is attached: we'd publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea on a revenue share, at no cost to you. It includes 12 months' exclusivity for those markets while we prepare the launch. We'd need it signed by Oct 20.

Noor
====

Hi Frederick,

Heads-up that the free Starter tier on your account ends on Oct 31. From Nov 1 the account moves to Team ($29/month) under your existing agreement, so phone and SMS paging keep working for your on-call rota. If you'd rather drop back to the free plan, reply and I'll downgrade you before then. Free has email alerts only, no paging.

Can you confirm either way?

Dana Whitfield
Customer Success, Pingwise
===

As discussed, the free tier covers alerts for 'Zombie Match 3D' and 'Harmony Games' on the app stores and socials. To switch it on, accept the terms in the dashboard and you're set. Nothing to pay.

Leah
===
Hi Frederick,

The SSL certificate on your game API domain expires on Oct 20. The renewal is $89 for the year. Reply to confirm and we'll reissue it; otherwise it lapses on the 20th.

Jonas
===

• Reserve *highest contrast and saturation* for characters.
• Avoid harsh shadows or strong highlights behind key gameplay areas.

• We do not see any app exceptions, they are all gone from first 3 levels.
• We did have some forced restarts, but only among people that started level 1, and did not finish level 1, and I believe a handful were company internal installs based out of Seattle ([PERSON_NAME_0036])
• We have noticed that There are restarts not captured by the "forced_kill_app" event, but instead we derived that There was a restart from a "user_session" and "play_login" event at strange times after the initial app launch. Also the fact that There are tutorial events prefixed with "bookmarked_xxx" which is only something that can trigger if someone have left the app (quit)
• So far out of 6 players observed that's not US installs for started level 1 but not finished level 1, at least 2 of them had some indicator of restarts, or having really abrupt last event. In a normal healthy quitting funnel, the last event is typically "user_engagement" (This is the event that Firebase use to measure session time). Any time the player does not have user_engagement as their last event, it's quite suspicious.
• For people that started level 2 but did not finish level 2 (3 observed). 2 of them had bookmarked tutorial events, meaning they restarted their app.
• For people that started level 3 but did not finish level 3 (11 observed), 2 are definitely suspicious and involving some restarts, the others all concentrated on this single step where we dim and spotlight the gold tile boost, but for some reason these people don't go beyond that step, it's almost as if the dimming/spotlight drove them away. This is highly suspicious still.
Action items:
• We have noticed that the FTUE can put you in a permanent stasis, albeit quite difficult. If you manage to get to the character tutorial, you upgrade sophie for the first time using your token (deducted from inventory), but you didn't finish that entire character tutorial (quit before the "let's go back and see what sophie can do now"), upon restart, your FTUE will error out and dim in a place unclickable, and it will happen doesn't matter how many restarts you have, you will be 100% stuck, forever. As a result of this, <@EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID> will be making most of the tutorial steps to be able to be clicked away, after a ~1 second pause. This is so that in the event where a dimming is done improperly in an unclickable part of the game, the click anywhere should at least give the players a chance to progress.
• We are also fixing the bookedmarked version of the tutorial. What this means is that currently if you were in level 2 wildcard tutorial, and you quit before you finish the level, on the restart, playing the same exact level will now trigger sophie's streak ability of +1 card, where as on the non bookmarked version of the tutorial, that ability is purposely disabled. Players can get stuck like this if they end up drawing the card sophie granted them, and if it's not a match, the game ends up in a loss.
• Basically anytime you consume something because the FTUE makes you do it, the gold/item is permanently deducted from the inventory. And if you manage to restart the app before fully completing that portion of the tutorial, the restarted tutorial will ask you to conduct the same action again, but it can potentially cause an error because you no longer have the gold/item to pay for that action. values: Quote for 12 rigged monster models ($6,400, 50% on kickoff)
Arthur told them we're keeping the art in-house and passing (Sep 19). Not contacted again.
Creative retainer proposal: $3,500/month from Oct 1, 3-month minimum; asked us to confirm by Oct 1
Declined in writing: not taking the retainer, please don't book the team for October.
ASO retainer proposal: $900/month from Oct 1; asked us to confirm by Oct 1
Declined in writing: not going ahead with the retainer, no need to send a contract.
Store listing localization quote: 12 languages, $2,640 on delivery; price holds to Oct 3; waiting for a PO
Declined in writing: not sending a PO, not going ahead.
Order form: 12-player moderated panel Oct 14, $1,200 prepaid; confirm by Oct 6
Declined in writing: not booking the Oct 14 panel.
Booth hold at Bay Area Indie Showcase (Oct 24): $4,800, $2,400 deposit due Oct 10
Declined in writing: please release the booth hold; no deposit coming.
Trailer music pack annual licence: $1,188 paid on signature; quote holds to Oct 15
Declined in writing: not taking the licence, no need to send it for signature.
UGC Studio pilot (HG-2291) hit 20-video cap; converts to Studio plan $1,800/month on Oct 16 unless cancelled in writing to the billing address by Oct 15
Cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io per the Paylane notice (Oct 1); told Priya we're not continuing after the pilot.
Pro order form: 4 seats, $149/month billed from Nov 1; answer wanted by mid-October
Declined in writing: not setting up Pro; free seat only.
Seattle Indie Expo pre-registration push (Nov 7): we pay travel/hotel for two (~$1,600) booked by Wishwave and invoiced to us; confirm by Oct 17
Declined in writing: can't cover the travel, so not taking part; please don't book anything.
30-day trial from Sep 19 moves to Growth $79/month on Oct 20 unless cancelled by Oct 19 (cancel by email to onboarding contact)
Cancelled in writing to Hana (onboarding contact): please cancel before the trial converts; no Growth plan.
November creator campaign: $8,000, 50% deposit on booking; bookings close Oct 31
Declined in writing: not booking the November slot.
Indie showcase slot Dec 5: $750 stand fee (call held with Robert, Sep 17)
Declined in writing: not taking the Dec 5 slot.
Nightly DB backups move to Standard $19/month at Oct 12 renewal; asked us to confirm
Confirmed in writing: keep the nightly backups running on Standard.
SSL cert for the game API domain expires Oct 20; renewal $89/year; reply to confirm
Confirmed in writing: please reissue the certificate.
Starter tier ends Oct 31; moves to Team $29/month from Nov 1 (paging) unless we downgrade
Confirmed in writing: stay on Team, keep phone/SMS paging.
Publishing LOI for Zombie Match 3D in Japan/Korea; revenue share, no cost; 12 months' exclusivity; sign by Oct 20
Told them it's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign.
Startup Program agreement: $25k credits, 36-month term, no charges; sign by Oct 31 (cohort closes)
Told them it's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign.
Holiday puzzle bundle participation agreement: no cost, licence of Domino Delights name/logo/art for 18 months; sign by Nov 1
Told them it's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign.
Southeast Asia publishing proposal for Domino Delights: 70/30 rev share, no upfront fee, 2-year exclusive term
Told them it's with our lawyers (ESG) first, then Leonard or Arthur to sign.
November puzzle week featuring agreement; no fees; accept in partner portal by an authorised signatory by Oct 24
Told them it's with Leonard or Arthur to accept in the portal.
Mutual NDA on ESG's template (2-year term) before the Oct 8 call; officer signature
Told them it's with Leonard or Arthur to sign (our template, no legal review needed).
Free tier brand monitoring; activation needs click-through terms accepted in the dashboard
Told them it's with Leonard or Arthur to accept the terms; keep setup on hold until then.
App embedding licence for two display fonts: $640 when ordered; quote valid to Jan 31, 2026
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Beta free through Jan 31, 2026, paid from Feb; asked for a 30-min feedback call
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Team trial free until Feb 1, 2026 ($8/user/month after); offered to add rest of team
Told them we'll pick it up in January; no team additions for now.
Full benchmark set $300/month from Feb 2026 if we subscribe (sample was free)
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Trailer VO quote $950 paid at booking; valid to Feb 28, 2026
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Free pilot slot in Feb 2026 for website demo widget; asked whether to hold it
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Pro $49/month from upgrade; free plan continues
Told them we'll stay on free and pick it up in January.
Startup trial free until Jan 12, 2026, then Growth $99/month unless cancelled before Jan 12; asked if we'll stay on
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
$10,000 credits reserved until Feb 28, 2026; asked activate now or later
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
2026 launch PR package: $1,200 when booked, any time before launch
Told them we'll pick it up in January.
Startup promo free until Jan 31, 2026, then $39/month unless cancelled; asked if we'll keep the scheduler
Told them we'll pick it up in January.

input.subject: Cancellation - workspace HG-2291 (UGC Studio) - Harmony Games
input.body:
Hello,

Per your notice of Sep 12 ("Workspace HG-2291: your pilot is ending"), Harmony Games Inc. is cancelling before the Studio plan starts. Please do not start the Studio plan ($1,800/month) on Oct 16, 2025, and do not bill us for workspace HG-2291 (UGC Studio) after the pilot ends on Oct 15, 2025.

Please confirm the cancellation in writing.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Co-founder, Harmony Games Inc.
frederick.stone@harmonygames.co

content.text: All 33 vendor answers plus the Paylane cancellation are sent. Next: the four ESG intake emails (one per agreement, per the intake checklist).

input.subject: Agreement intake: Kinetic Arcade - publishing LOI (Zombie Match 3D, Japan/Korea)
input.body:
Hi ESG team,

Please open a matter for the following agreement for Harmony Games Inc.

- Company and agreement: Kinetic Arcade - letter of intent to publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea on a revenue share.
- Term and automatic renewal: 12 months from signature; no automatic renewal stated.
- Exclusivity / licence of our IP: 12 months' exclusivity for Japan and Korea while they prepare the launch.
- What it costs us: nothing (revenue share, no fees to Harmony Games).
- Date they need it by: Oct 20, 2025.
- Who would sign it: Leonard Hayes.

Contact at Kinetic Arcade: Noor Haddad. I can forward the LOI on request.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.subject: Agreement intake: Lumencloud - Startup Program agreement
input.body:
Hi ESG team,

Please open a matter for the following agreement for Harmony Games Inc.

- Company and agreement: Lumencloud - Startup Program agreement ($25,000 in cloud credits).
- Term and automatic renewal: 36 months from signature; no automatic renewal stated.
- Exclusivity / licence of our IP: none stated.
- What it costs us: nothing while the credits last (credits usable over 36 months).
- Date they need it by: Oct 31, 2025 (cohort closes).
- Who would sign it: Arthur Blake.

Contact at Lumencloud: Aiden Clarke. I can forward the agreement on request.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.subject: Agreement intake: Bundlehouse - holiday puzzle bundle participation agreement (Domino Delights)
input.body:
Hi ESG team,

Please open a matter for the following agreement for Harmony Games Inc.

- Company and agreement: Bundlehouse - participation agreement for their holiday puzzle bundle, featuring Domino Delights (revenue share on bundle sales).
- Term and automatic renewal: the licence runs 18 months; no automatic renewal stated.
- Exclusivity / licence of our IP: licence for Bundlehouse to use Domino Delights' name, logo and art in bundle marketing for 18 months. No exclusivity stated.
- What it costs us: nothing (no cost to join).
- Date they need it by: Nov 1, 2025.
- Who would sign it: Leonard Hayes.

Contact at Bundlehouse: Freya Olsen. I can forward their deck on request.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.subject: Agreement intake: Lanternfly Publishing - Southeast Asia publishing deal (Domino Delights)
input.body:
Hi ESG team,

Please open a matter for the following agreement for Harmony Games Inc.

- Company and agreement: Lanternfly Publishing - publishing Domino Delights in Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines): localization, store featuring and UA on a 70/30 revenue share after store fees. We have their proposal deck; the agreement itself hasn't been sent yet.
- Term and automatic renewal: 2-year term; automatic renewal not stated in the proposal.
- Exclusivity / licence of our IP: exclusive for Southeast Asia; publishing implies a licence of the game in the region.
- What it costs us: no upfront fee.
- Date they need it by: no date given (they want it for their Q4 slate).
- Who would sign it: Leonard Hayes.

Contact at Lanternfly Publishing: Wen Halvorsen. I can forward the proposal deck on request.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

content.text: All 31 contacts are in. Last step: the reply to Leonard on his thread.

input.body:
Leonard,

The backlog is done. I went by the guardrails doc and your Monday change (travel/event costs count as cash even when a partner books them and bills us). Everyone who was waiting on us got a written answer today, the contacts are in Contacts, and the log is in the Q4 commitments folder: "Q4 commitments log" https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/6a38fe5aaeeb0dad/edit (34 companies).

What we're keeping (Arthur's keep-running list):
- Vaultline: nightly DB backups move to Standard, $19/month, renews Oct 12
- Certwell: SSL cert for the API domain, $89/year, renews Oct 20
- Pingwise: on-call paging stays on Team, $29/month from Nov 1

Waiting on you or Arthur to sign (all on the Harmony Games board To Do list):
Going to ESG first (intake emails sent today, one per agreement, you and Arthur cc'd):
- Kinetic Arcade: Japan/Korea publishing LOI, 12 months' exclusivity. Needed by Oct 20.
- Lumencloud: Startup Program agreement, $25k credits, 36-month term. Needed by Oct 31.
- Bundlehouse: holiday bundle participation agreement, 18-month licence of Domino Delights' name and art. Needed by Nov 1.
- Lanternfly Publishing: SEA publishing for Domino Delights, 2-year exclusive. No date given; they've only sent the deck so far.
No ESG review needed, just an officer:
- Playfuse: mutual NDA on ESG's template. Needed before the Oct 8 call.
- Orbit Store: November featuring agreement, to be accepted in their partner portal. Needed by Oct 24.
- Markward: free-tier click-through terms. No deadline.

For your awareness, the rest:
- Ended: Brightlane, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor Events (booth released before the Oct 10 deposit), Soundvault, Framewell, Wishwave (because of the travel change), Streamcast Talent and Spotlight Fest. Two cancellations were in writing: the Clipforge pilot (to Paylane billing before it rolls into $1,800/month on Oct 16) and the Reviewly trial (before it moves to $79/month on Oct 20).
- Parked for the Jan 5 review: Glyphworks, Quillcraft, Loopnote, Benchmarkly, Driftwood Audio, Tilecast, Echohall, Retainly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam and Hootline. I have a reminder for each on Jan 5. Retainly's trial converts on Jan 12, so that one needs deciding at the review.
- Already answered: Motive Forge (Arthur passed on Sep 19), so we didn't write to them again.
- Left off the log: Nova Rewards withdrew its offer on Sep 23.

Fred

content.text:
The vendor and partner backlog is cleared and I've replied to Leonard on his thread. I decided each company using his runway guardrails doc, plus the change he posted in #executives on Monday: travel and event costs count as cash even when a partner books them and bills us. That covers 34 companies.

**Decisions**
- **Keep (3), all on Arthur's keep-running list:**
  - Vaultline backups: $19/mo, renews Oct 12.
  - Certwell SSL certificate: $89/yr, renews Oct 20.
  - Pingwise paging: $29/mo from Nov 1.
- **Waiting on Leonard or Arthur to sign (7):**
  - **ESG has to review first (4):** Kinetic Arcade (exclusivity, needed by Oct 20), Lumencloud (36-month term, by Oct 31), Bundlehouse (18-month licence of Domino Delights' name and art, by Nov 1) and Lanternfly (2-year exclusive, no date). I sent ESG one intake email per agreement, with Leonard and Arthur cc'd.
  - **Officer signature only (3):** Playfuse NDA (before the Oct 8 call), Orbit Store featuring agreement (by Oct 24) and Markward's click-through terms (no deadline).
- **Ended (12):**
  - These would have cost cash before January: Brightlane, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor Events, Soundvault, Framewell, Streamcast Talent, Spotlight Fest.
  - Wishwave ended because of Leonard's travel change.
  - Two trials were set to start billing on their own, so I cancelled them in writing. Clipforge's notice said to write to Paylane billing by Oct 15, before the $1,800/mo plan starts. Reviewly would have moved to $79/mo on Oct 20.
- **Parked for the Jan 5 review (11):** Glyphworks, Quillcraft, Loopnote, Benchmarkly, Driftwood Audio, Tilecast, Echohall, Retainly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam, Hootline. Retainly's trial turns paid on Jan 12, so it needs a decision at the review.
- **Already answered (1):** Arthur turned down Motive Forge on Sep 19, so I didn't write to them again.
- **Left out of the log:** Nova Rewards withdrew its offer. I also skipped cold pitches nobody answered, and everything Leonard named as out of scope (ad networks, PlayableX, Craftsman+, Singular, investors, Mattel).

**What's in place**
- **Log:** "Q4 commitments log" is in your Q4 commitments folder, with one row per company and the README's columns.
- **Replies:** 33 vendors have a written answer, and the Clipforge cancellation went to Paylane billing.
- **Board:** 7 signing cards are on the Harmony Games To Do list, titled with the company name and with due dates where there is one.
- **Calendar:** 11 all-day reminders on Jan 5, one per parked company.
- **Contacts:** I added 31 vendor contacts with the company in the job field. Aiden (Lumencloud), Noor (Kinetic Arcade) and Leah (Markward) were already there.

**Decisions you may want to check**
- **Signers:** Leonard's notes only say "Leonard or Arthur", so I picked who signs in the ESG emails and on the cards. I put Leonard on Kinetic Arcade, Bundlehouse and Lanternfly, and Arthur on Lumencloud. The vendors were only told "Leonard or Arthur", so changing this means updating ESG and the cards.
- **Lanternfly:** I routed it through ESG even though they've only sent a proposal deck, because the deck already says 2-year exclusive.
- **Spotlight Fest:** it looked like a cold pitch, but Robert held a call with them on Sep 17, so I counted it as engaged and declined it.
